title: Apache Thrift Client/Server Configuration Example
description: Example showing how to configure and start a Thrift server and client with transport and protocol selections

examples.name: Java Server Setup
examples.description: Setting up a non-blocking Thrift server in Java with compact protocol

examples.name: Python Client Setup
examples.description: Connecting to a Thrift service from Python using binary protocol over TCP

examples.name: Go Service Definition
examples.description: Service implementation pattern in Go generated from Thrift IDL

code_pattern.ping: func (p *CalculatorHandler) Ping(ctx context.Context) (err error) { return nil }
code_pattern.add: func (p *CalculatorHandler) Add(ctx context.Context, num1 int32, num2 int32) (int32, error) { return num1 + num2, nil }

examples.name: Node.js Client Setup
examples.description: Connecting to a Thrift service from Node.js

code_pattern.require: const thrift = require('thrift'); const Calculator = require('./gen-nodejs/Calculator');
code_pattern.connect: const connection = thrift.createConnection('localhost', 9090, { transport: thrift.TFramedTransport, protocol: thrift.TCompactProtocol })

protocol_options.name: TBinaryProtocol
protocol_options.description: Default binary protocol; fast but not compact

protocol_options.name: TCompactProtocol
protocol_options.description: Compact binary with variable-length integers; recommended

transport_options.name: TFramedTransport
transport_options.description: 4-byte length-prefixed framing; required for non-blocking servers

server_options.name: TThreadedSelectorServer
server_options.description: Multi-selector non-blocking; recommended for high concurrency
